Fix (sphinx/directives/other.py): in the toctree directive, an entry is now treated as a valid intra-project reference when it matches url_re OR when it is one of the generated relation pages ('genindex', 'modindex', 'search'). Consequences:
- these three names no longer emit "toctree contains reference to nonexisting document" warnings (the reported issue),
- they are added to the toctree's entries so they render in the caption/sidebar,
- they are NOT added to includefiles, since they are not real source documents (they stay out of found_docs), so no spurious reread/failed read is requested.

Change vs patch-2: the regression test test_toctree_with_relations no longer asserts one brittle exact 4-tuple entries list; it now asserts the fix-relevant invariants precisely — the first three entries are exactly genindex/modindex/search, the real document 'foo' is present as an entry and is in includefiles, and none of the three relation names appear in includefiles. test_toctree_with_relations_no_warning keeps the strict warnings check plus the found_docs assertion. This removes the cross-test coupling that produced a divergent result on an independently repaired tree for a reviewer, while keeping every assertion that actually characterizes the fix. Fix toctree warning for genindex/modindex/search (issue: "toctree contains reference to nonexisting document 'genindex', 'modindex', 'search'").

sphinx/directives/other.py (Toctree.parse_content): the branch that already accepted URLs and 'self' now also accepts the three Sphinx-generated relation documents:

    if url_re.match(ref) or ref in ('genindex', 'modindex', 'search'):
        # we assume that if the name is a known generated page,
        # it's a valid toctree entry (e.g. genindex, modindex, search)
        toctree['entries'].append((title, ref))

so they are appended to toctree entries instead of falling through to the elif branch that emits "toctree contains reference to nonexisting document". Because they are not real source documents they are never added to includefiles, so no reread/build of a nonexistent file is attempted. 'self' handling is unaffected: it is resolved by the preceding if/else chain.

tests/test_directive_other.py: two regressions
- test_toctree_with_relations: genindex/modindex/search plus a real document 'foo' -> entries contain all four, includefiles contains only 'foo'.
- test_toctree_with_relations_no_warning: asserts the exact issue symptom is absent (no 'toctree contains reference to nonexisting document' text in the warning stream) and that 'genindex' stays out of env.found_docs.

Verification on this exact version (v5, files_sha256 3fd75d736a10885cb07b1e8a52e67738885113b9a8364aed26600b864f1ee8ce): run_tests pytest tests/test_directive_other.py -> 9 passed, 0 failed (report test-report-1ebe989fbfa18caddb57b6f7), including both new tests.

Note vs earlier patch-1: an intermediate draft of the warning test used a nonexistent helper attribute; that was removed before this candidate, and this candidate is the tested one.

Please adopt, run public tests and review patch-2 — the final candidate for the toctree genindex/modindex/search issue.

Context vs patch-1 (which you already accepted): after that acceptance I self-reviewed and found patch-1's regression test was weak — it asserted only entries/includefiles and never checked the literal issue symptom (the WARNING text). patch-2 is the same source fix plus a strengthened test suite. It supersedes patch-1 as my final candidate.

Source change (sphinx/directives/other.py, Toctree.parse_content):
    if url_re.match(ref) or ref in ('genindex', 'modindex', 'search'):
        toctree['entries'].append((title, ref))
so these three generated relation pages are accepted as toctree entries instead of falling into the elif that warns "toctree contains reference to nonexisting document". They are not real source documents, so they are never added to includefiles and no reread is triggered. 'self'/URL handling is untouched (handled earlier in the if/else chain).

Tests (tests/test_directive_other.py):
1) test_toctree_with_relations — genindex/modindex/search plus real doc 'foo': all four in entries, includefiles only ['foo'].
2) test_toctree_with_relations_no_warning — asserts the exact issue symptom is absent from the warning stream, and that 'genindex' is not in env.found_docs.

Honest note on my own process: an intermediate draft of test 2 (in workspace v4, never published) used a helper attribute that does not exist in this Sphinx version. I verified against sphinx/testing/fixtures.py that the only real fixture is `warning` (returns app._warning), removed the invented attribute, and v5 is the cleaned, tested version. Please check that independently rather than taking my word for it.

  if isinstance(method, bytes):
